acts.desc: Story of a romance that began in a mental hospital. Sometimes, the line between crazy and not crazy is blurry; certain behavior could mean either thing.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Susanna Kaysen reads from her account of living at McLean psychiatric hospital for about two years, starting when she was eighteen. Her book, Girl, Interrupted, describes daily life on the ward.
acts.title: Girl, Interrupted

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Dr Patricia Deegan hears voices in her head. She's a psychologist and she believes that the only way mental health workers can really understand what their patients go through is if they hear voices themselves. So she and a few other voice-hearers put together a tape for mental health workers. It's a simulation of what the voices say and how they sound. She says that she and others actually hear the voices, as if they are voices in the room. Dr Deegan's organization is the National Empowerment Center.
acts.title: Guided By Voices

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: David Sedaris tells a story from his boyhood, when a voice inside his head commanded him to lick every light switch and tap his forehead with his heel. It's from his book Naked.
acts.title: Plague Of Tics

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Joel Lovell tells a story about working in a mental institution, and what it's like when it feels like your grip on the keys isn't so steady.
acts.title: You Don't Have To Be Crazy To Work Here, But It Helps
